newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MORE QUESTIONS RAISED ABOUT COLSTON'S EXPENSES
More concerns have been raised in parliament about Independent Senator Mal Colston's use of parliamentary entitlements.
Victorian Labor Senator, Robert Ray, has raised questions about a Queensland Senator allegedly harassing foreign embassies, and flying to Perth, only to stay in the aiport lounge and fly back.

Senator Colston says the allegations are ridiculous and scurrilous. Senator Ray, who's led the Opposition assault on the Labor defector claims there's very little mis-use of Parliamentary entitlements, a view Senator Colston agrees with.
NITSCHKE PREDICTS ANTI-EUTHANASIA LAW WILL BE CARRIED

Darwin pro-euthanasia doctor, Phillip Nitschke, says he expects the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia law to be overturned. The Senate is due to receive a report next week from a Senate committee examining euthanasia, and will debate Kevin Andrews' anti-voluntary euthanasia bill later this month.
Dr Nitschke says he expects the Andrews' bill will be carried, but not by much.
SYDNEY SITE CONSIDERED FOR NUCLEAR REPROCESSING

The federal government is considering Lucas Heights in Sydney's south, as one of the sites for a nuclear reprocessing plant. The proposal is one of three options to go before Cabinet, which is due to discuss a solution to the stockpile of nuclear waste stored at Sydney's nuclear science facility.
The facility, which operates a research reactor, will run out of space for its spent fuel rods by the end of next year.
FISCHER SAYS NO BASIS FOR ANTHRAX TRADE BAN
The Deputy Prime Minister says there's absolutely no basis for a South Korean ban on Australia's processed meats and milk because of the Anthrax break-out in Victoria.

Australia's been asked to stop all shipments until South Korean quarantine officials in Victoria, have finished their investigation. The officials are expected to report to the South Korean National Assembly in the next few days.

Tim Fischer says there's been some misinformation about the outbreak, and Australia is doing all it can to have the ban lifted. So far 192 cattle on 83 dairy farms have died in the outbreak, which the Natural Resources Department says is slowing down and should soon be controlled.
TOURISM INDUSTRY BLASTS PLANS TO SCRAP SURVEY
Federal Government plans to scrap a key tourism survey have been blasted by the tourism industry.
The Tourism Council of Australia's Bruce Baird, says plans to dump the Survey of Tourist Accommodation could jeopardise the industry's ability to judge future accommodation needs.

Mr Baird says the survey includes details on accommodation such as where visitors are from, how long they're staying, and what standard of accommodation they're using. He says that information is vital because it assists in the building of new accommodation.
GRETLEY MINE LAWYER RAISES PROSECUTION QUERY
Counsel Assisting the Inquiry into the New South Wales Gretley mine disaster has raised concerns about the prosecution policies of the Department of Mineral Resources.

Four men were killed in the accident on November the 14th last year. Counsel Assisting, David Kirby QC, told the inquiry yesterday that a review of reports into serious occurrences at New South Wales mines by Inspectors with the Department found no prosecutions had been launched against mine operators over many years.
PERTH INVESTIGATING ANOTHER HEPATITIS CASE

Health authorities in Perth are investigating another confirmed Case of Hepatitis-A. It's believed the person could have eaten contaminated oysters from Wallis Lake, on the New South Wales mid-north coast.
The oysters have been blamed for hundreds of cases of hepatitis-A in New South Wales, Queensland, Victoria and South Australia.
GRAND PRIX COULD BE HIT BY STRIKES
Melbourne public transport workers meet tomorrow, amid looming strike action during the Grand Prix this weekend.
After a break-down in negotiations between the Public Transport Union and the Government, the union has issued another threat about walking off the job for the entire weekend.
Yesterday's meeting, over wages and conditions, ended with the union accusing the Kennett Government of provoking a strike. - - - -
QUEENSLAND RIVER LEVELS FALL
In North-West Queensland, police say river levels at Cloncurry are falling this morning. They had feared the Cloncurry River would reach another flood peak last night, but it failed to eventuate.
